title: warpfront/hipfire RDNA-native inference and evidence mechanisms

sources.license: MIT/Apache-2.0 bundle with NOTICE and per-surface provenance caveats; pinned submodule license not inspected

observations: Hipfire treats RDNA-native inference as a fail-closed evidence system: physical admission, cache/session identity, retained-command safety, architecture-isolated kernels, and route/hash-bound certification outrank isolated throughput.

The pinned tree contains strict memory admission, transactional adaptive-KV handoff, safe session-prefix reuse, retained-command replay, typed super-op lowering, and architecture-specific fused kernels.
Benchmark and Redline doctrine separate measurement from production admission and bind claims to fixture, artifact, route, source, daemon, registry, profile, contract, and PM4 identities.
The large investigation corpus and retained FAILED kernels make negative knowledge a durable product surface rather than disposable scratch.
Open device-mesh, source-aware loading, collective-aware execution, and partial-resource rollback work are directions, not shipped facts at the pin.
This pass is clean-room inspiration only: no Hipfire code was copied. Direct integration requires file-level provenance, NOTICE, generated/vendor, and submodule-license review.

candidates.effect: Reserve native inference memory against startup peak and steady-state physical capacity before execution.
candidates.outcome: Existing FAK issue already owns aggregate unified-memory byte and pressure admission; no duplicate filed.

candidates.effect: Reuse prompt prefixes only under monotonic session identity while excluding active generations.
candidates.outcome: Existing serving-baseline issue already includes prefix reuse and paged KV; retain Hipfire's identity/exclusion invariants as acceptance criteria.

candidates.effect: Make adaptive-KV ownership handoff transactional and resettable.
candidates.outcome: FAK has transactional cache-geometry rollback but not yet the same shipped adaptive-tier seam; watch under the existing KV serving issue.

candidates.effect: Certify benchmarks with fixture, artifact, route, source, daemon, registry, profile, contract, and command identity separated from admission.
candidates.outcome: FAK already has a benchmark authority and witnessed receipt discipline; no parallel framework.

candidates.effect: Retain measured failed native optimizations with operating-envelope and diagnosis evidence.
candidates.outcome: FAK already preserves negative native evidence through SOTA, claim, benchmark, and dated-note surfaces.

candidates.effect: Select host-capability-aware gates and emit typed machine-readable receipts.
candidates.outcome: FAK/DOS already route typed gates and receipts; no duplicate implementation.

candidates.effect: Roll back partially allocated native model resources transactionally on load failure.
candidates.outcome: Upstream partial-device rollback is itself emerging and FAK host-file cleanup does not prove device-resource rollback; wait for a concrete FAK native allocation seam and witness.
